In this Unreleased full interview from November 2018, Yella Beezy sits down with DJ Vlad for a candid VladTV interview after surviving a Dallas freeway shooting that left his G-Wagon hit 23 times and sent him to the hospital with multiple gunshot wounds. The “That’s On Me” rapper reflects on staying calm, seeing his young son, watching his BET Awards performance from recovery, and why Boosie, Kevin Gates and Yo Gotti urged him to move differently after the attack.

Beezy also talks hometown hate, Young Greatness, Marley G, comparisons to Tupac’s Las Vegas shooting, and the realities of being a rapper in the public eye. He breaks down the star-packed “That’s On Me” remix with 2 Chainz, Jeezy, T.I., Boosie, Rich The Kid and Trapboy Freddy, plus his Hitco joint venture with L.A. Reid and debut album Ain’t No Goin Back featuring Kevin Gates, Lil Baby and Tokyo Jetz.

John Franzese Jr. sits down with VladTV to discuss a pivotal period in his life: graduating high school as his father, John Franzese Sr., returned home after nine years in prison. Franzese Jr. recalls staying away from drugs and alcohol as a teenager, while growing close to his brother Michael Franzese and figures around Andrew’s crew, including Jojo Russo and Chuckie Russo.  

As his father faced intense law enforcement scrutiny and later a parole violation, Franzese Jr. began visiting him alone in jail and learned how conversations had to be handled carefully through coded language. He also describes driving his father to Brooklyn, attending a meeting at “Junior’s” house with captains present, and how his young age sometimes offered cover amid the family’s legal pressure. A firsthand look at family loyalty, prison communication, and Colombo crime family history.

In this VladTV interview, Marlow Bates and Tamir Stanfield revisit the events that led to their 1985–1986 arrests and the major cases that changed their lives. They discuss alleged “people in high places,” the FBI’s attention on their Baltimore operation, claims of a drug conspiracy, wiretaps, and why they say authorities used witnesses and murder accusations to get them off the streets. Bates recalls being picked up over ammunition purchases before facing several homicide-related charges, while Stanfield breaks down his own federal case, New York connection, and courtroom battles involving his attorney. The two describe separate murder and conspiracy trials, disputed testimony, and receiving double-life sentences while still in their early 20s. From Baltimore streets to New York’s Apollo Theater backdrop, this conversation offers a raw look at crime, law enforcement, federal investigations, and the justice system through their perspective.

Rene Enriquez sits down with Vlad to revisit the controversy surrounding *American Me*, the Edward James Olmos film about the Mexican Mafia, also known as La Eme. Enriquez explains how he first heard the movie was filming in Ramona Gardens, why he sought the script through contacts tied to the production, and how a letter to Olmos ended up being reported to the FBI. He breaks down which scenes he believes reflected real people and which moments he says took dramatic license, including depictions involving Cheyenne Gardner, prison politics, and the conflict with Nuestra Familia. The conversation also turns deeply personal as Enriquez discusses childhood abuse, how trauma influenced his later violence, and his work mentoring young offenders at Ironwood. A candid discussion of true crime, prison culture, gang history, Hollywood accuracy, and rehabilitation.

Tito “TJ” Dominguez sits down with Vlad to recount the tense buildup to his federal arrest, including how he says he gathered intelligence from inside the grand jury process and played “cat and mouse” with surveillance teams outside his Florida mansion. Dominguez describes taunting suspected DEA agents with champagne, calling 911 on their parked car, and earning the nickname “Mad Dog” as multiple agencies closed in.

The conversation details the early-morning raid involving DEA, ATF, FBI and IRS Criminal Division investigators, plus the role of agents like Jim Crow and Organized Crime Task Force figure Fred Short. Dominguez also breaks down the 848 CCE (Continuing Criminal Enterprise) charge, comparisons to RICO, alleged smuggling of marijuana and cocaine into Florida, and indictments tied to South Florida, Georgia, New York, Detroit and the Bahamas. He reflects on the “historical conspiracy” case, solitary confinement, forfeiture battles, and the deal that changed his future.
